sci:arg.name: Container ID
sci:arg.sci:help:
The ID specified here should be referenced in any Protocol Function components that will automatically insert content into this container.

To guarantee interoperability among browsers, IDs should start with a letter and consist only of letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, colons, and periods.

sci:arg.name: Format
sci:arg.sci:help:
Specifies formatting to be applied to this element. Editing this parameter opens the Format Dialog.

Depending on what this Format is being applied to, options may include:

  • Font settings (e.g., Color, Size, Bold, Italic, Underline)
  • Border settings (e.g., Color, Style, Width)
  • Background settings (Color, Image)
  • Alignment settings
  • etc.

Notes:

  • Only options that are relevant for this specific Format parameter will be displayed.
  • Background Image: Allows you to select a background image for the reporting element. This image must be accessible to the Pipeline Pilot server. For example, there are some example images in the apps\scitegic\generic\dataroot\data\Images folder in your Pipeline Pilot installation (shortcut is "generic\Images" folder). To use your own images, you need to upload them to a location such as your userdir or jobdir. An easy way to do this is to use the Binary Reader component to read the file, and the Binary Writer component to save it to the chosen location. Supported image types include .gif, .jpg, .png, and .bmp.

sci:arg.name: Position
sci:arg.sci:help:
Specifies how this element is positioned. Editing this parameter opens the Position dialog, which enables you to change margins, paddings, width, and height.

If the Overflow Behavior is set to "Resize Container", any width and height information will be ignored, as the container will resize itself to its contents.

sci:arg.name: Overflow Behavior
sci:arg.sci:help:
How the container should treat oversized content inserted into the container:

  • Show scrollbars as necessary: If the content placed inside the container is larger than the size of the container (if an exact width or height are specified), then scrollbars will be shown to allow the user to scroll through all content.
  • Clipped: If the content placed inside the container is larger than the size of the container (if an exact width and height are specified), then any content overflowing the container will be clipped off, and no scrollbars will appear.
  • Resize to Content: Resizes the container to tightly fit the current content (also applies to initial content). Any width and height information specified in the Position parameter will be ignored.

sci:arg.name: Links and Actions
sci:arg.sci:help: Links and actions to be applied to the report element produced by this component.

sci:arg.name: Link Target
sci:arg.sci:help: Sets this element as the destination for links from other elements in the report. The value of Link Target can be text or a property name, and should match the value of Link in another report component. In the resulting report, when the element with Link is clicked, the element with the matching Link Target is brought to the top of the report page.

sci:arg.name: Tooltip
sci:arg.sci:help: An optional tooltip for this reporting element.

sci:arg.name: HTML Attributes
sci:arg.sci:help: Defines attributes for the reporting element. These attributes can be used by JavaScript code that is embedded in or included by the HTML report. One very common attribute is "id" which allows access to the element using the document.getElementById(id) method. Event handlers such as "onclick" and "onmouseover" are also common attributes.

sci:arg.name: Column Settings
sci:arg.sci:help: Column settings control how the element appears when it is used inside a table.

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Header Text
sci:arg.sci:help: When the element is used within a Table component, this parameter sets the text displayed at the top of its column.

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Header Format
sci:arg.sci:help:
When used in a table, this parameter sets the format of the text displayed at the top of its column.

Editing this parameter opens the Format Dialog. Options that can be changed by this parameter include Font, Font Size, Bold, Italic, Underline, and Color.

Notes:
Examples of available formatting options:
  • Font Size: Sets font size
  • Color: Sets font color

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Header Position
sci:arg.sci:help: When the element is used within a Table component, this parameter sets the position of the text displayed at the top of its column.

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Cell Format
sci:arg.sci:help:
When used in a table, this parameter sets the format of the cells in the column.

Editing this parameter opens the Format Dialog. Options that can be changed by this parameter include Font, Font Size, Bold, Italic, Underline, and Color.

Notes:
Examples of available formatting options:
  • Font Size: Sets font size
  • Color: Sets font color

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Cell Position
sci:arg.sci:help: When the element is used within a Table component, this parameter sets the position of the cells in the column.

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Adds a container (<div> tag) that can be updated with content generated by another protocol, using AJAX

Use this component to create an area in a report (a "container") where any existing content can be replaced with the results of another protocol without refreshing the rest of the report. Use this component in conjunction with the Protocol Function component to provide AJAX functionality in reports.

Alternatively, use the container to generate <div> elements in a report that can be manipulated via JavaScript.

The Protocol Function component specifies a protocol to run when the user takes an action such as clicking a button in the original report. When that action happens, the results of that protocol (a table, a chart, etc.) will be placed into the container defined by the Dynamic Content Container, replacing anything that is currently present. To link a Protocol Function component to this one, set its Dynamic Content Container ID to match the Container ID on this component. Multiple Protocol Function components may update the same container, and multiple pairs of Dynamic Content Container and Protocol Function components can be used in a single report.

When a protocol containing a Dynamic Content Container is run to generate a report, the container initially functions very much like a paragraph component. Any reporting content on data records piped in will be displayed inside the container. This content can then be updated using the AJAX functionality.

The container can also be used as a general box for content, as it supports the specification of fixed width and height and provides a means to specify how oversized content is handled.

Notes:

  • This component is for use in HTML reports only.
  • The value of the Container ID is output as an ID attribute. ID values should be unique within a report.
  • Dynamic Content Containers can be nested.

See Also:

  • Report Design Essentials
  • Interactive Reporting and Form Design
One or more data records containing reporting objects
A data record representing the container is sent to the pass port.

sci:arg.sci:help: The original path within the database of this component.
sci:arg.sci:value: Components\Reporting and Visualization\Reporting\Web Application Development\HTML Elements\Dynamic Content Container

  • Clipped: If the content placed inside the container is larger than the size of the container (if an exact width and height are specified), then any content overflowing the container will be clipped off, and no scrollbars will appear.
  • Resize to Content: Resizes the container to tightly fit the current content (also applies to initial content). Any width and height information specified in the Position parameter will be ignored.

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Adds a container (<div> tag) that can be updated with content generated by another protocol, using AJAX

Use this component to create an area in a report (a "container") where any existing content can be replaced with the results of another protocol without refreshing the rest of the report. Use this component in conjunction with the Protocol Function component to provide AJAX functionality in reports.

Alternatively, use the container to generate <div> elements in a report that can be manipulated via JavaScript.

The Protocol Function component specifies a protocol to run when the user takes an action such as clicking a button in the original report. When that action happens, the results of that protocol (a table, a chart, etc.) will be placed into the container defined by the Dynamic Content Container, replacing anything that is currently present. To link a Protocol Function component to this one, set its Dynamic Content Container ID to match the Container ID on this component. Multiple Protocol Function components may update the same container, and multiple pairs of Dynamic Content Container and Protocol Function components can be used in a single report.

When a protocol containing a Dynamic Content Container is run to generate a report, the container initially functions very much like a paragraph component. Any reporting content on data records piped in will be displayed inside the container. This content can then be updated using the AJAX functionality.

The container can also be used as a general box for content, as it supports the specification of fixed width and height and provides a means to specify how oversized content is handled.

Notes:

  • This component is for use in HTML reports only.
  • The value of the Container ID is output as an ID attribute. ID values should be unique within a report.
  • Dynamic Content Containers can be nested.

See Also:

  • Report Design Essentials
  • Interactive Reporting and Form Design
One or more data records containing reporting objects
A data record representing the container is sent to the pass port.

sci:arg.name: Component Path
sci:arg.sci:help: The original path within the database of this component.
sci:arg.sci:value: Components\Reporting and Visualization\Reporting\Web Application Development\HTML Elements\Dynamic Content Container

sci:arg.name: Container ID
sci:arg.sci:help:
The ID specified here should be referenced in any Protocol Function components that will automatically insert content into this container.

To guarantee interoperability among browsers, IDs should start with a letter and consist only of letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, colons, and periods.

sci:arg.name: Format
sci:arg.sci:help:
Specifies formatting to be applied to this element. Editing this parameter opens the Format Dialog.

Depending on what this Format is being applied to, options may include:

  • Font settings (e.g., Color, Size, Bold, Italic, Underline)
  • Border settings (e.g., Color, Style, Width)
  • Background settings (Color, Image)
  • Alignment settings
  • etc.

Notes:

  • Only options that are relevant for this specific Format parameter will be displayed.
  • Background Image: Allows you to select a background image for the reporting element. This image must be accessible to the Pipeline Pilot server. For example, there are some example images in the apps\scitegic\generic\dataroot\data\Images folder in your Pipeline Pilot installation (shortcut is "generic\Images" folder). To use your own images, you need to upload them to a location such as your userdir or jobdir. An easy way to do this is to use the Binary Reader component to read the file, and the Binary Writer component to save it to the chosen location. Supported image types include .gif, .jpg, .png, and .bmp.

sci:arg.name: Position
sci:arg.sci:help:
Specifies how this element is positioned. Editing this parameter opens the Position dialog, which enables you to change margins, paddings, width, and height.

If the Overflow Behavior is set to "Resize Container", any width and height information will be ignored, as the container will resize itself to its contents.

  • Clipped: If the content placed inside the container is larger than the size of the container (if an exact width and height are specified), then any content overflowing the container will be clipped off, and no scrollbars will appear.
  • Resize to Content: Resizes the container to tightly fit the current content (also applies to initial content). Any width and height information specified in the Position parameter will be ignored.

sci:arg.name: Copy File To Images Folder
sci:arg.sci:help:
If true the file will be copied to a folder where other images in the report, such as molecules and charts, are stored. This makes reports easier to view offline, as all supporting files are referenced by relative URIs. It also guarantees that reports can not be changed after generation, in the event that source images are updated.

If false, reports will use a CGI script to download files from their original location on the server. This makes reports easier to distribute, as supporting files are referenced by absolute URI, and do not have to be distributed.

This option is only relevant for HTML reports and does not apply to SVG images, which are always copied to the images folder.

sci:arg.name: Link
sci:arg.sci:help:
An optional parameter specifying a link for the reporting element produced by this component. The Link value can be an internal report link or an external URL.

  • Internal: A string that points to a Link Target in the report. Both the Link and Link Target values need to match for an internal link to work.
  • External: A string that points to an external URL such as 'http://www.sitename.com', 'ftp://www.sitename.com', or a file URL. A file URL can be in one of these forms:
    • 'file:///C:/.../scitegic root/.../document.pdf' - when using an absolute path within the Pipeline Pilot installation folder
    • 'file://///machine_name/C/.../document.pdf' - when using a Windows UNC path visible to the Pipeline Pilot server
    • 'file:///relative_path/document.pdf' - when using a path, relative to @SciTegicRoot
    • 'file://machine_name.domain_name.com/C/.../document.pdf' - when using a path with a fully qualified machine name

Example: To create a link from a combination of a property and static text, create a valid PilotScript expression. For example, if you have internal web pages linking to research projects that have addresses of the form: http://mydomain.com/ProjectID, where ProjectID is the actual project ID, and also a local property on the datastream, you would use:

'http://mydomain.com' . ProjectID

as the value for Link.

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Adds an image to a report

Reads an image file and places it in a report. Supported image formats include PNG, JPEG, and SVG.

Source specifies the location of the image file.

SVG files will be converted to bitmaps when included in PDF and Office reports. HTML reports containing SVG images can only be accessed via the webserver, i.e., the SVG will will not load correctly if the report is loaded via a file:// URI. For this reason, it is generally a good idea to output these reports in the job directory when using a HTML Report Writer.

TIFF images can be included in all reports. In HTML reports, TIFF images will be output using the <embed> element, which will cause your default TIFF viewer (e.g., AlternaTIFF) to be activated.

See Also:

  • For creating images from data in a protocol (local or global properties) use Image from Data.
  • Report Design Essentials
A data record representing the image is sent to the pass port.

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Adds a container (<div> tag) that can be updated with content generated by another protocol, using AJAX

Use this component to create an area in a report (a "container") where any existing content can be replaced with the results of another protocol without refreshing the rest of the report. Use this component in conjunction with the Protocol Function component to provide AJAX functionality in reports.

Alternatively, use the container to generate <div> elements in a report that can be manipulated via JavaScript.

The Protocol Function component specifies a protocol to run when the user takes an action such as clicking a button in the original report. When that action happens, the results of that protocol (a table, a chart, etc.) will be placed into the container defined by the Dynamic Content Container, replacing anything that is currently present. To link a Protocol Function component to this one, set its Dynamic Content Container ID to match the Container ID on this component. Multiple Protocol Function components may update the same container, and multiple pairs of Dynamic Content Container and Protocol Function components can be used in a single report.

When a protocol containing a Dynamic Content Container is run to generate a report, the container initially functions very much like a paragraph component. Any reporting content on data records piped in will be displayed inside the container. This content can then be updated using the AJAX functionality.

The container can also be used as a general box for content, as it supports the specification of fixed width and height and provides a means to specify how oversized content is handled.

Notes:

  • This component is for use in HTML reports only.
  • The value of the Container ID is output as an ID attribute. ID values should be unique within a report.
  • Dynamic Content Containers can be nested.

See Also:

  • Report Design Essentials
  • Interactive Reporting and Form Design
One or more data records containing reporting objects
A data record representing the container is sent to the pass port.

sci:arg.name: Component Path
sci:arg.sci:help: The original path within the database of this component.
sci:arg.sci:value: Components\Reporting and Visualization\Reporting\Web Application Development\HTML Elements\Dynamic Content Container

sci:arg.name: Container ID
sci:arg.sci:help:
The ID specified here should be referenced in any Protocol Function components that will automatically insert content into this container.

To guarantee interoperability among browsers, IDs should start with a letter and consist only of letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, colons, and periods.

sci:arg.name: Format
sci:arg.sci:help:
Specifies formatting to be applied to this element. Editing this parameter opens the Format Dialog.

Depending on what this Format is being applied to, options may include:

  • Font settings (e.g., Color, Size, Bold, Italic, Underline)
  • Border settings (e.g., Color, Style, Width)
  • Background settings (Color, Image)
  • Alignment settings
  • etc.

Notes:

  • Only options that are relevant for this specific Format parameter will be displayed.
  • Background Image: Allows you to select a background image for the reporting element. This image must be accessible to the Pipeline Pilot server. For example, there are some example images in the apps\scitegic\generic\dataroot\data\Images folder in your Pipeline Pilot installation (shortcut is "generic\Images" folder). To use your own images, you need to upload them to a location such as your userdir or jobdir. An easy way to do this is to use the Binary Reader component to read the file, and the Binary Writer component to save it to the chosen location. Supported image types include .gif, .jpg, .png, and .bmp.

sci:arg.name: Position
sci:arg.sci:help:
Specifies how this element is positioned. Editing this parameter opens the Position dialog, which enables you to change margins, paddings, width, and height.

If the Overflow Behavior is set to "Resize Container", any width and height information will be ignored, as the container will resize itself to its contents.

sci:arg.name: Overflow Behavior
sci:arg.sci:help:
How the container should treat oversized content inserted into the container:

  • Show scrollbars as necessary: If the content placed inside the container is larger than the size of the container (if an exact width or height are specified), then scrollbars will be shown to allow the user to scroll through all content.
  • Clipped: If the content placed inside the container is larger than the size of the container (if an exact width and height are specified), then any content overflowing the container will be clipped off, and no scrollbars will appear.
  • Resize to Content: Resizes the container to tightly fit the current content (also applies to initial content). Any width and height information specified in the Position parameter will be ignored.

sci:arg.name: Links and Actions
sci:arg.sci:help: Links and actions to be applied to the report element produced by this component.

sci:arg.name: Link Target
sci:arg.sci:help: Sets this element as the destination for links from other elements in the report. The value of Link Target can be text or a property name, and should match the value of Link in another report component. In the resulting report, when the element with Link is clicked, the element with the matching Link Target is brought to the top of the report page.

sci:arg.name: Tooltip
sci:arg.sci:help: An optional tooltip for this reporting element.

sci:arg.name: HTML Attributes
sci:arg.sci:help: Defines attributes for the reporting element. These attributes can be used by JavaScript code that is embedded in or included by the HTML report. One very common attribute is "id" which allows access to the element using the document.getElementById(id) method. Event handlers such as "onclick" and "onmouseover" are also common attributes.

sci:arg.name: Column Settings
sci:arg.sci:help: Column settings control how the element appears when it is used inside a table.

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Header Text
sci:arg.sci:help: When the element is used within a Table component, this parameter sets the text displayed at the top of its column.

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Header Format
sci:arg.sci:help:
When used in a table, this parameter sets the format of the text displayed at the top of its column.

Editing this parameter opens the Format Dialog. Options that can be changed by this parameter include Font, Font Size, Bold, Italic, Underline, and Color.

Notes:
Examples of available formatting options:
  • Font Size: Sets font size
  • Color: Sets font color

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Header Position
sci:arg.sci:help: When the element is used within a Table component, this parameter sets the position of the text displayed at the top of its column.

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Cell Format
sci:arg.sci:help:
When used in a table, this parameter sets the format of the cells in the column.

Editing this parameter opens the Format Dialog. Options that can be changed by this parameter include Font, Font Size, Bold, Italic, Underline, and Color.

Notes:
Examples of available formatting options:
  • Font Size: Sets font size
  • Color: Sets font color

sci:arg.name: Column Settings Cell Position
sci:arg.sci:help: When the element is used within a Table component, this parameter sets the position of the cells in the column.

sci:arg.name: Script
sci:arg.sci:help: Type the JavaScript in the scripting window. It will be included in the HTML report.

sci:arg.name: Output Location
sci:arg.sci:help:
Determines whether the value of Script is output in the header or body of the output document.

For functions that are called by event handlers (set using the HTML Attributes parameter on other components), scripts should be placed in the header. Any duplicated scripts will be removed.

Functions that create content (e.g., using document.write()) need to be output in the document body, and the script will be written at the position of the component.

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Adds JavaScript to an HTML Report

Type the JavaScript into Script. The script will be included in either the header or body of the HTML report, depending on Output Location. Functions defined in the script are accessible using HTML Attributes, which is present in many Reporting Collection components.

Pipeline Pilot Globals may be used in JavaScript as shown in the following example: 

function showUserName() {
  alert('$(UserName)');
}

Calling the showUserName function will show an alert window containing the name of the user that ran the protocol.

Not valid for PDF reports.

See Also:

  • Report Design Essentials
  • Interactive Reporting and Form Design
A single data record containing the JavaScript to be included in the HTML report.

sci:arg.name: Expression
sci:arg.sci:help: The PilotScript expression used to filter the data.
sci:arg.sci:value: @xml is defined and @xml ne '' and @filelist is eq ''

sci:arg.name: Initial Expression
sci:arg.sci:help:
An expression evaluated only when the component is first initialized (when the first data record enters).

Since there is no data available at initialization time, only expressions referencing local or global properties are allowed.

sci:arg.name: Final Expression
sci:arg.sci:help:
An expression evaluated only when the component is finalized (once the last data record has passed).

Since there is no data available at finalization time, only expressions referencing local or global properties are allowed.

sci:arg.name: Keep Calculated Properties
sci:arg.sci:help: Allows any properties that were calculated in "Expression" to be included with the exiting record. Otherwise, these properties are removed after the evaluation is complete.

sci:arg.name: ComponentAttributes
sci:arg.sci:help: Component Attributes

sci:arg.name: OnDataTypeError
sci:arg.sci:help: When an expected data type is not found during processing: Halt: Terminate the execution of the network Fail: Continue execution of the network, passing data out the Fail(red) port Pass: Continue execution of the network, passing data out the Pass(green) port

sci:arg.name: OnGeneralError
sci:arg.sci:help: When an recoverable error occurs during processing: Halt: Terminate the execution of the network Fail: Continue execution of the network, passing data out the Fail(red) port Pass: Continue execution of the network, passing data out the Pass(green) port

sci:arg.name: CustomErrorText
sci:arg.sci:help: Custom Error Message

sci:arg.name: ExpressionVersion
sci:arg.sci:help: Version of expression parser to use.

sci:arg.sci:help: The user who registered this component.

sci:arg.sci:help: The date this component was registered.

sci:arg.name: ComponentAutoDisplayName
sci:arg.sci:help: Automatically update the component display name when the "Expression" property is changed. This feature is turned off after the user manually changes the display name of the component in Protocol workspace.

sci:arg.name: DerivedFrom
sci:arg.sci:help: The component this component is based upon.

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Passes data records for which a PilotScript expression evaluates to True

For each incoming data record, the PilotScript statements in Expression are evaluated. If the last statement in the expression evaluates to True or non-zero, the record is sent out the Pass port. Otherwise it is sent out the Fail port.

Notes:

  • To initialize global variables such as counters, use Initial Expression.
  • To clean up global variables or calculate final results use Final Expression.
  • Parameters on Custom Manipulators do not become global variables that can be accessed via @ParameterName syntax. They must be accessed by using the Parameter('ParameterName') function or by using token substitution via $(ParameterName) syntax.
Data records for which the final expression in the PilotScript evaluates to True or non-zero
Data records for which the final expression in the PilotScript evaluates to False or zero

sci:arg.sci:help: Local Component Identifier

sci:arg.name: Component Path
sci:arg.sci:help: The original path within the database of this component.
sci:arg.sci:value: Components\Data Access and Manipulation\Property Filters\Custom Filter (PilotScript)

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help: Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allow the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running local or remote. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required.'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: Comma separated list of maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:help: Run subprotocol on grid engine if available.
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Queue Name
Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Grid Options
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Queue Name
sci:arg.sci:help: Select the queue name on the grid to submit jobs to. Leave blank to use default queue name.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Grid Options
sci:arg.sci:help: Use this to specify grid engine specific command line parameters to the job submission command. Leave blank to use defaults.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Preserve Order
sci:arg.sci:help: Whether to preserve the order of the data as it enters and leaves the remote subprotocol.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Tempfiles
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma delimited list of global properties, each of which will automatically hold the name of a file in the job's temporary folder, whose name is guaranteed to be unique.

For each global name, an additional global is created (with the suffix _Filename) that hold just the leaf file name of the temporary file.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top level global property list and is accessible from all protocols, but may collide with another property of the same name.

Scoping global properties to the subprotocol where they are used is highly recommended.

Use a subprotocol to collapse one or more components into a single item. Open a subprotocol to view or edit its contents.

Tip: Any component can be made into a shortcut, so that the latest version is always used. For more information, see Creating Shortcuts.

sci:arg.name: Script
sci:arg.sci:help:
The Python script to execute. Pipeline Pilot executes the following three subroutines:
  • onInitialize: the subroutine that executes before the first data record is processed.
  • onProcess: the subroutine that executes for each data record.
  • onFinalize: the subroutine that executes after the last data record has been processed.

The ctxt function parameter (and the context facade wrapping it), give access to the environment the component operates in. Data like global variables and the component parameters are accessible via this object.
The dr function parameter and its data facade provide access to the data passed into the component.
sci:arg.sci:value:
import swigpython3 as pilotbase import pilotpython import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET import os
def onInitialize(ctxt): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) return pilotpython.READY_FOR_INPUT_OR_NEW_DATA
def onProcess(ctxt, dr): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) data = pilotpython.DataRecord(dr) props = data.getProperties() # Get the PropertyCollection
try: source_xml_path = context.getComponentParameters().get("Source").getValue().getString().strip() context.debugMessage(f"Source path received: {source_xml_path}") abs_path=context.constructAbsolutePath(source_xml_path) context.debugMessage(f"abs_path:{abs_path}") tree = ET.parse(abs_path) root = tree.getroot()
file_names = [] file_locations = [] name_locations = {}
for generic in root.findall('generic'): eln_value_elem = generic.find('ELN_value') if eln_value_elem is not None: eln_value = eln_value_elem.text if eln_value and '\\' in eln_value: file_name = os.path.basename(eln_value) file_location = eln_value name_locations[file_name]=file_location file_names.append(file_name) file_locations.append(file_location) section_name = generic.find('XML_title') location = generic.find('ELN_value') location = location.text section_name = section_name.text location = location[0:location.rfind('\\')] location = location[location.find('users'):] # Define properties using the PropertyCollection props.defineStringProperty("location", location) # Define properties using the PropertyCollection props.defineStringArrayProperty("FileNames", file_names) props.defineStringProperty("SectionName", section_name) #context.debugMessage(f"FileNames defined: {file_names}") context.debugMessage(str(name_locations)) props.defineStringArrayProperty("FileLocations", file_locations) props.defineHashTableProperty("file_loc", name_locations)
except Exception as e: context.debugMessageError(f"Exception occurred while processing XML: {str(e)}")
return pilotpython.READY_FOR_INPUT_OR_NEW_DATA
def onFinalize(ctxt): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) return None

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Runs a Python 3 script on the server

The Script parameter already contains a script skeleton with the three functions onInitialize(ctxt), onProcess(ctxt, dr) and onFinalize(ctxt). Those already provide access to the component's environment and the data accessible to it at runtime. To implement the desired functionality, just import any required 3rd party modules, and write functions and glue code to transfer data in and out of Pipeline Pilot. To make 3rd party modules available for import, see the paragraph about Integration of 3rd party modules.

Integration of 3rd party modules

Integration of 3rd party modules is fairly straightforward.
In the case of a pure-Python module, use the PythonPath parameter to specify the module's location.
For modules with binary dependencies (.pyd or .so files), e.g. numpy, or scipy, the solution is platform dependent.
For Linux, one can simply define a shellscript containing an updated LD_LIBRARY_PATH and copy it into the $scitegic/linux_bin/env.d folder. The Pipeline Pilot server will automatically execute that script when creating protocol processes. E.g. a dependency on intel's math library could be resolved with this approach. A more sophisticated version could involve the creation of a custom package, containing a set of specific components and such a script.
For Windows, no action may be necessary. In case the 3rd party module is part of an existing Anaconda distribution on the server, it's possible that a protocol fails with DLL load failed: The specified module could not be found., e.g. when using pillow or numpy. In that case, a fix may simply be to download the offending module's wheel, and reinstalling it into Anaconda with Anaconda's pip. If that is not successful, rebuilding the module using the Python shipped with Pipeline Pilot and integrating it into a Pipeline Pilot package should fix this issue.

Integration of other Pipeline Pilot packages

If your script requires Python modules contained in other Pipeline Pilot packages, use the Use Package parameter. If a Pipeline Pilot package is listed here, the system will query that package's package.conf file for its Python directive and read all applicable PythonPath entries. Packages have to be listed using the vendor/package notation.

See Also:

  • Dynamic Java (on Server)
  • Python Development Guide
  • Python Scripting Component API

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Applies a PilotScript expression to each data record

PilotScript is the native scripting language in Pipeline Pilot. It is based on PL/SQL and allows you to query or alter the properties on data records. For example, the expression:

A := 10;
creates a property named "A" and sets the value to "10".

For each incoming data record the PilotScript statements in Expression are evaluated.

Notes:

  • To initialize global variables such as counters, use Initial Expression.
  • To clean up global variables or calculate final results use Final Expression.
  • Parameters on Custom Manipulators do not become global variables that can be accessed via @ParameterName syntax. They must be accessed by using the Parameter('ParameterName') function or by using token substitution via $(ParameterName) syntax.

See Also:

  • For more information on PilotScript, see PilotScript Overview.
  • To use PilotScript to filter data records use Custom Filter (PilotScript).

sci:arg.name: Text
sci:arg.sci:help: The text, or property containing the text, to be shown as an entry in the list box.

sci:arg.name: Value
sci:arg.sci:help:
The value that will be submitted for each item in the list. If not specified, the value of Text will be submitted.

Notes:

  • When working with array data in PilotScript expressions use the special property "CurrentArrayIndex" to access the array element that is currently being processed. For example, to multiply the values of the array property, "Foo", by 2, use:

    Foo[CurrentArrayIndex] * 2

    If you omit [CurrentArrayIndex], only the first element of the array will be used.

    If the PilotScript expression is just a property name, you do not need to use "CurrentArrayIndex".

  • Due to inconsistent input value attribute handling by various browsers, it is recommended that the Value parameter not include leading or trailing whitespace. Depending on the browser, this whitespace may be omitted when the form is submitted. A possible workaround is to flank the entire value with a special character that can then be stripped when the input value is processed in the work protocol.

sci:arg.name: Number of Displayed Rows
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of rows to show in the list box. If the number of items exceeds the number of rows, then the list box will contain a scroll bar.

To create a drop-down list, set the number of rows to 1.

sci:arg.name: Allow Multiple Selections
sci:arg.sci:help: If true, multiple selections can be made in the list box. Otherwise, only one entry can be selected.

sci:arg.name: Selected
sci:arg.sci:help:
An optional PilotScript expression evaluating to True or False that determines if the current entry is pre-selected in the list box. For example, if the Text parameter is set to a property 'MyPet' and you want to have a value 'Cat' selected, then do the following:

MyPet eq 'Cat';

If you want the last item in a single selection list box to be pre-selected, simply enter True.

Notes:

  • When working with array data in PilotScript expressions use the special property "CurrentArrayIndex" to access the array element that is currently being processed. For example, to multiply the values of the array property, "Foo", by 2, use:

    Foo[CurrentArrayIndex] * 2

    If you omit [CurrentArrayIndex], only the first element of the array will be used.

    If the PilotScript expression is just a property name, you do not need to use "CurrentArrayIndex".

sci:arg.name: Parameter to Map
sci:arg.sci:help: The name of a parameter on the target protocol that this component's value should be mapped to.

sci:arg.name: Format
sci:arg.sci:help:
Specifies formatting to be applied to this element. Editing this parameter opens the Format Dialog.

Depending on what this Format is being applied to, options may include:

  • Font settings (e.g., Color, Size, Bold, Italic, Underline)
  • Border settings (e.g., Color, Style, Width)
  • Background settings (Color, Image)
  • Alignment settings
  • etc.

Notes:

  • Only options that are relevant for this specific Format parameter will be displayed.
  • Background Image: Allows you to select a background image for the reporting element. This image must be accessible to the Pipeline Pilot server. For example, there are some example images in the apps\scitegic\generic\dataroot\data\Images folder in your Pipeline Pilot installation (shortcut is "generic\Images" folder). To use your own images, you need to upload them to a location such as your userdir or jobdir. An easy way to do this is to use the Binary Reader component to read the file, and the Binary Writer component to save it to the chosen location. Supported image types include .gif, .jpg, .png, and .bmp.

sci:arg.name: Position
sci:arg.sci:help: Specifies how this element is positioned. Editing this parameter opens the Position dialog, which enables you to change margins, paddings, width, and height.

sci:arg.name: Aggregate Data
sci:arg.sci:help:
Determines how List Box(es) will be created from data records:

  • True: A single List Box will be created with all values of Text (i.e., for all data records).
  • False: A List Box will be created for each data record, holding the value(s) of Text on each record. This is useful when Text contains arrays of values, and you want a List Box for each array.
  • Based on Input Data: The number of values of Text on the first data record will determine if the component will aggregate data or not. If there is more than one value the component will not aggregate data, otherwise it will.

sci:arg.sci:help: Sets this element as the destination for links from other elements in the report. The value of Link Target can be text or a property name, and should match the value of Link in another report component. In the resulting report, when the element with Link is clicked, the element with the matching Link Target is brought to the top of the report page.

One very common attribute is "id" which allows access to the element using the document.getElementById(id) method. Event handlers such as "onclick" and "onmouseover" are also common attributes.

sci:arg.sci:value: Adds a list box form element to a report

Used to select one or more items from a list, to be passed to the work protocol. Single or multi-select can be set. If multiple values are selected, they are passed as an array.

Text accepts properties that have single values as well as array data, in which case a list item will be created for each array element. Depending on the value of Aggregate Data either a single list box or a list box for each data record will be created.

You can set the number of rows to be displayed. If the number of rows is less than the number of values to be displayed, then a vertical scroll bar is automatically added. To create a drop-down list, set the number of rows to be displayed to 1.

See Also:

  • Report Design Essentials
  • Interactive Reporting and Form Design
Data records containing entries to be shown in a List Box.
A data record representing the List Box and its associated data.

sci:arg.name: Overflow Behavior
sci:arg.sci:help:
How the container should treat oversized content inserted into the container:

  • Show scrollbars as necessary: If the content placed inside the container is larger than the size of the container (if an exact width or height are specified), then scrollbars will be shown to allow the user to scroll through all content.
  • Clipped: If the content placed inside the container is larger than the size of the container (if an exact width and height are specified), then any content overflowing the container will be clipped off, and no scrollbars will appear.
  • Resize to Content: Resizes the container to tightly fit the current content (also applies to initial content). Any width and height information specified in the Position parameter will be ignored.

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Adds a container (<div> tag) that can be updated with content generated by another protocol, using AJAX

Use this component to create an area in a report (a "container") where any existing content can be replaced with the results of another protocol without refreshing the rest of the report. Use this component in conjunction with the Protocol Function component to provide AJAX functionality in reports.

Alternatively, use the container to generate <div> elements in a report that can be manipulated via JavaScript.

The Protocol Function component specifies a protocol to run when the user takes an action such as clicking a button in the original report. When that action happens, the results of that protocol (a table, a chart, etc.) will be placed into the container defined by the Dynamic Content Container, replacing anything that is currently present. To link a Protocol Function component to this one, set its Dynamic Content Container ID to match the Container ID on this component. Multiple Protocol Function components may update the same container, and multiple pairs of Dynamic Content Container and Protocol Function components can be used in a single report.

When a protocol containing a Dynamic Content Container is run to generate a report, the container initially functions very much like a paragraph component. Any reporting content on data records piped in will be displayed inside the container. This content can then be updated using the AJAX functionality.

The container can also be used as a general box for content, as it supports the specification of fixed width and height and provides a means to specify how oversized content is handled.

Notes:

  • This component is for use in HTML reports only.
  • The value of the Container ID is output as an ID attribute. ID values should be unique within a report.
  • Dynamic Content Containers can be nested.

See Also:

  • Report Design Essentials
  • Interactive Reporting and Form Design
One or more data records containing reporting objects
A data record representing the container is sent to the pass port.

sci:arg.name: Component Path
sci:arg.sci:help: The original path within the database of this component.
sci:arg.sci:value: Components\Reporting and Visualization\Reporting\Web Application Development\HTML Elements\Dynamic Content Container

sci:arg.name: Text
sci:arg.sci:help:
A PilotScript expression that evaluates to the text to render in this object. This expression has access to global data and any properties (or calculable properties) on the incoming data record. Also, you can provide text as static (quoted) strings.

Notes:

  • To specify a property name that includes whitespace characters, use the property() PilotScript function, e.g., if the property name is "Profit Margin" use:

    property('Profit Margin')

  • When specifying columns for an in-line table, the expression you enter here (often simply a property name), will be the default column header. To explicitly set the column header, use Column Settings > Header Text.

sci:arg.name: Link
sci:arg.sci:help:
An optional parameter specifying a link for the reporting element produced by this component. The Link value can be an internal report link or an external URL.

  • Internal: A string that points to a Link Target in the report. Both the Link and Link Target values need to match for an internal link to work.
  • External: A string that points to
    • an external URL such as 'http://www.sitename.com', 'ftp://www.sitename.com', or
    • a file URL, such as 'file:///relative_path/document.pdf' - using a path relative to @SciTegicRoot

Example: To create a link from a combination of a property and static text, create a valid PilotScript expression. For example, if you have internal web pages linking to research projects that have addresses of the form: http://mydomain.com/ProjectID, where ProjectID is the project ID data property on the datastream, you would use:

'http://mydomain.com/' . ProjectID

as the value for Link.

sci:arg.name: Tempfiles
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma delimited list of global properties, each of which will automatically hold the name of a file in the job's temporary folder, whose name is guaranteed to be unique.

For each global name, an additional global is created (with the suffix _Filename) that hold just the leaf file name of the temporary file.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top level global property list and is accessible from all protocols, but may collide with another property of the same name.

Scoping global properties to the subprotocol where they are used is highly recommended.

sci:arg.name: Reporting
sci:arg.sci:help: This group contains parameters specific to protocols containing Reporting components.

sci:arg.name: Reporting Stylesheet
sci:arg.sci:help: Specifies the name of a Stylesheet to be used by this protocol if any of the Reporting components have a Style selected in the Format and Position parameters.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help: Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allow the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running local or remote. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help:
Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.

 

Note: In an expression inside the subprotocol you can identify the category property name as:

      parentproperty('RunToCompletion Categorize Using')

And so to access the value of this property on the current data record, use:

      property(parentproperty('RunToCompletion Categorize Using'))
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allows the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running locally or remotely. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option with care, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. Generally speaking, it yields improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma-separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (that is, server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be useful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid

sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: A comma-separated list of the maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.</br></br>For non-Grid Engine job, the number of jobs will be limited to the value for the maximum number of simultaneous subprotocol jobs as defined in the Admin Console even if this value is higher than the value entered here or '*'.</br></br>For Grid Engine jobs, the number of jobs will be limited to the value for the maximum number of simultaneous subprotocol grid jobs as defined in the Admin Console even if this value is higher than the value entered here or '*'.</br></br>

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Grid Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
This is an array of command line options to send to the Grid engine submit command.

If you just include one line, whatever you enter will be sent "as is" to the submission command.


Example - Just sending options directly to command line - PBS

-l procs=16 -l walltime=08:00:00 -A PROJECTID


There are a number of parameters that Pipeline Pilot will translate to the correct command line options for whichever supported Grid Engine you are using.


Example - Supported parameters

Account=<Project/Account name>

Maximum Execution Time=<HH:MM:SS> hours, minutes, seconds - LSF ignores seconds

Number of Cores=<16>

Number of GPUs=<4>

Parallel Environment=<The Parallel Environment to use> - Only needed for SGE

Other=<Additional Parameters sent directly to submit command line>


Any of these options can be commented out by placing a # in front of them.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid');

sci:arg.name: Tempfiles
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma-delimited list of global properties, each of which is automatically populated with the name of a file in the job's temporary folder, which always has a unique name.

For each global name, an additional global is created (with the suffix _Filename) that hold only the leaf file name of the temporary file.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Separate property names with commas. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top-level global property list and is accessible from all subprotocols, but breaks the encapsulation of the subprotocol and may collide with another property of the same name.

Therefore, you should always declare a new global property in the DeclareLocal parameter, to minimize the scope of the global property to the subprotocol where it is used.

The example DeclareLocal value below creates 3 global properties in the subprotocol scope. Note that you can initialize the declared global value with a scalar value using the ":=" syntax, as shown. You can surround text string values with quotes to aid clarity.

    SubP_Counter := 0, SubP_NameHash, SubP_TitleText:="Sample 1"

sci:arg.sci:value: Passes data records for which a PilotScript expression evaluates to True

For each incoming data record, the PilotScript statements in Expression are evaluated. If the last statement in the expression evaluates to True or non-zero, the record is sent out the Pass port. Otherwise it is sent out the Fail port.

Notes:

  • To initialize global variables such as counters, use Initial Expression.
  • To clean up global variables or calculate final results use Final Expression.
  • Parameters on Custom Manipulators do not become global variables that can be accessed via @ParameterName syntax. They must be accessed by using the Parameter('ParameterName') function or by using token substitution via $(ParameterName) syntax.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top level global property list and is accessible from all protocols, but may collide with another property of the same name.

Scoping global properties to the subprotocol where they are used is highly recommended.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help: Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.

sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allow the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running local or remote. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required.'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: Comma separated list of maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Authentication Options
sci:arg.sci:help: Options for user credentials when the HTTP server requires authentication.

sci:arg.name: Authentication Method
sci:arg.sci:help:
Controls how the components authenticate when connecting to the Notebook. Contact your AEP server administrator for information on the appropriate method to use in your environment.

  • Use Username and Password Parameters: Use the values provided by the component's Username and Password parameters. This will perform a Notebook login and use the retrieved Notebook session token for authentication in all downstream components. The username and password provided should be for a valid Notebook user.
  • Use Pipeline Pilot Credentials: Use the username and password that were provided when the user logged into Pipeline Pilot. This can be used if the Notebook server supports Windows Integrated Authentication, and the user credentials for both Notebook and AEP are synchronized (this is usually the case if both servers authenticate against the same domain).
  • Use Pipeline Pilot Session Token: The current user's Pipeline Pilot session token is used by components for authentication. This is the best choice if the Notebook server and AEP server credentials are synchronized, and only when running protocols on the AEP server that is paired with the Notebook server.
  • Use Notebook Session Token: An existing Notebook session token can be supplied in the Existing Notebook Session Token parameter along with the username of the user for which this session token was generated. This method is useful when running the protocols from the Notebook client, in which case, the session token and the username are passed to the protocol as parameter values at run time. It may be useful to set the authentication to "Use Username and Password Parameters" while developing and testing such a protocol from the Pipeline Pilot client, and switching to "Use Notebook Session Token" when the protocol is deployed and tested from the Notebook client.

sci:arg.name: Authentication Method Username
sci:arg.sci:help:
The username used if authentication is needed for an HTTP server.

If the Authentication Method is set to 'Use Username and Password Parameters', then this parameter can be filled in to provide authentication information to the remote server. If 'Use Session Token' authentication is used, then this needs to be the username for which the session token was generated.

If the Authentication Method is set to 'Use Pipeline Pilot Credentials' the value of this parameter, if non-blank, will be used in conjunction with the password entered when logging in to the Pipeline Pilot client.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("To enable, set Authentication Method to 'Use Pipeline Pilot Credentials', 'Use Username and Password Parameters' or 'Use Notebook Session Token'"); Parameter('Authentication Method') eq 'Use Username and Password Parameters' or Parameter('Authentication Method') eq 'Use Notebook Session Token' or Parameter('Authentication Method') eq 'Use Pipeline Pilot Credentials'

sci:arg.name: Authentication Method Password
sci:arg.sci:help: The Notebook password of the username specified in the Notebook Username parameter.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("To enable, set Authentication Method to 'Use Username and Password Parameters'"); Parameter('Authentication Method') eq 'Use Username and Password Parameters'

sci:arg.name: Existing Notebook Session Token
sci:arg.sci:help:
This allows for an existing session token to be provided if the Authentication Method parameter is set to 'Use Notebook Session Token' or 'Use Pipeline Pilot Session Token'.
  • Use Notebook Session Token: session token is required and should be one that was generated for the user with the username specified in the Username parameter. This is usually the case if running the protocol as an action from the Notebook client.
  • Use Pipeline Pilot Session Token: session token is optional. If no session token is provided, the session token for the user running the protocol is used.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("To enable, set Authentication Method to 'Use Notebook Session Token'"); Parameter('Authentication Method') eq 'Use Notebook Session Token' or Parameter('Authentication Method') eq 'Use Pipeline Pilot Session Token'

sci:arg.name: Additional Request Headers
sci:arg.sci:help: Optional headers to add to each call made to the Notebook API. On the HTTP request, the data sent in the headers is HeaderName: HeaderValue. There is a limit of maximum three additional headers that can be provided. By default, these headers will also be used for the call this component makes to the Hub (only if this Pipeline Pilot server is registered with a Hub). To prevent the headers being used on the Hub connection, add a boolean parameter called UseAdditionalHeadersForHub to this component and set it to False.

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value:
Creates a global Notebook connection details object with the given name. This global contains authentication information and can be used by name in all components that connect to the Notebook API, relieving the user from entering authentication information in multiple components in a protocol.

Authentication can be done in four different ways:

  • using the Pipeline Pilot credentials for a Notebook server that supports Windows Integrated Authentication
  • Using a valid Pipeline Pilot session token. This can be an existing session token that is passed in, or the current session token for the user running the protocol. This authentication method will only work if the Notebook server is configured to accept tokens from the Pipeline Pilot server that has generated the session token being used.
  • Using the Notebook username and password. In this case, a Notebook session token is obtained from the login service and used for authentication.
  • Using a Notebook session token. This can be passed in as a protocol parameter value using the %SESSIONTOKEN% variable if the protocol is executed from the Notebook client's Actions toolbox. Please note that the user name of the user that this session token was generated for needs to also be passed in.

sci:arg.name: Initial Expression

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Passes data records for which a PilotScript expression evaluates to True

For each incoming data record, the PilotScript statements in Expression are evaluated. If the last statement in the expression evaluates to True or non-zero, the record is sent out the Pass port. Otherwise it is sent out the Fail port.

Notes:

  • To initialize global variables such as counters, use Initial Expression.
  • To clean up global variables or calculate final results use Final Expression.
  • Parameters on Custom Manipulators do not become global variables that can be accessed via @ParameterName syntax. They must be accessed by using the Parameter('ParameterName') function or by using token substitution via $(ParameterName) syntax.

sci:arg.sci:help: The submission status of the experiment.

sci:arg.name: Signing Status
sci:arg.sci:help:
The signing status of the experiment. This depends on the type of project assigned to the experiment. There are three types of projects:
  • No signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - no author signature needed
  • Author signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - waiting for author signature
    • Signed - no witness signature needed
  • Author and witness signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - waiting for author signature
    • Signed - waiting for witness signature
    • Rejected by witness
    • Witnessed

sci:arg.sci:help: The experiment type. Enter one per row.

sci:arg.name: Edited Since Date
sci:arg.sci:help: Only retrieve experiments edited since this date.

sci:arg.name: Include Invalid Experiments
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, experiments that have an Errata section with the value Invalid will be included in the query results. The default is to not include these results in any query.

sci:arg.name: Only Current User Experiments
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, only experiments where the current user is the author are retrieved from the database. Note that if a user query is passed in the filter for a user other than the current user, no results will be retrieved.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('This choice is not available when filtering by experiment number.'); not (Parameter('Filter By') eq 'Experiment Number' and Parameter('Filter Type') eq 'Equals')

sci:arg.name: Return Simple Section Data
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, simple section data will be returned with the experiment. This data includes the section ID, type and position in the experiment for all sections. Section content will not be returned.

sci:arg.name: Maximum
sci:arg.sci:help: Maximum number of experiments to retrieve. If blank, all experiments that match the query will be retrieved.
