sci:arg.name: Tempfiles
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma delimited list of global properties, each of which will automatically hold the name of a file in the job's temporary folder, whose name is guaranteed to be unique.

For each global name, an additional global is created (with the suffix _Filename) that hold just the leaf file name of the temporary file.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top level global property list and is accessible from all protocols, but may collide with another property of the same name.

Scoping global properties to the subprotocol where they are used is highly recommended.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help: Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allow the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running local or remote. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required.'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: Comma separated list of maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:help: Run subprotocol on grid engine if available.

Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Grid Options
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Grid Options
sci:arg.sci:help: Use this to specify grid engine specific command line parameters to the job submission command. Leave blank to use defaults.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid');

Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required.'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: Comma separated list of maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Initial Expression
sci:arg.sci:help:
An expression evaluated only when the component is first initialized (when the first data record enters).

Since there is no data available at initialization time, only expressions referencing local or global properties are allowed.

sci:arg.name: Final Expression
sci:arg.sci:help:
An expression evaluated only when the component is finalized (once the last data record has passed).

Since there is no data available at finalization time, only expressions referencing local or global properties are allowed.

sci:arg.name: Keep Calculated Properties
sci:arg.sci:help: Allows any properties that were calculated in "Expression" to be included with the exiting record. Otherwise, these properties are removed after the evaluation is complete.

sci:arg.name: OnGeneralError

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Passes data records for which a PilotScript expression evaluates to True

For each incoming data record, the PilotScript statements in Expression are evaluated. If the last statement in the expression evaluates to True or non-zero, the record is sent out the Pass port. Otherwise it is sent out the Fail port.

Notes:

  • To initialize global variables such as counters, use Initial Expression.
  • To clean up global variables or calculate final results use Final Expression.
  • Parameters on Custom Manipulators do not become global variables that can be accessed via @ParameterName syntax. They must be accessed by using the Parameter('ParameterName') function or by using token substitution via $(ParameterName) syntax.
Data records for which the final expression in the PilotScript evaluates to True or non-zero

sci:arg.sci:help: Search by text keyword. If multiple keywords are required, add them on separate lines.

sci:arg.sci:help: The submission status of the experiment.

sci:arg.name: Signing Status
sci:arg.sci:help:
The signing status of the experiment. This depends on the type of project assigned to the experiment. There are three types of projects:
  • No signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - no author signature needed
  • Author signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - waiting for author signature
    • Signed - no witness signature needed
  • Author and witness signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - waiting for author signature
    • Signed - waiting for witness signature
    • Rejected by witness
    • Witnessed

sci:arg.sci:help: The experiment type. Enter one per row.

sci:arg.name: Edited Since Date
sci:arg.sci:help: Only retrieve experiments edited since this date.

sci:arg.name: Include Invalid Experiments
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, experiments that have an Errata section with the value Invalid will be included in the query results. The default is to not include these results in any query.

sci:arg.name: Only Current User Experiments
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, only experiments where the current user is the author are retrieved from the database. Note that if a user query is passed in the filter for a user other than the current user, no results will be retrieved.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('This choice is not available when filtering by experiment number.'); not (Parameter('Filter By') eq 'Experiment Number' and Parameter('Filter Type') eq 'Equals')

sci:arg.name: Return Simple Section Data
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, simple section data will be returned with the experiment. This data includes the section ID, type and position in the experiment for all sections. Section content will not be returned.

sci:arg.name: Maximum
sci:arg.sci:help: Maximum number of experiments to retrieve. If blank, all experiments that match the query will be retrieved.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('This choice is not available when filtering by experiment number.'); not (Parameter('Filter By') eq 'Experiment Number' and Parameter('Filter Type') eq 'Equals')

sci:arg.name: Tempfiles
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma delimited list of global properties, each of which will automatically hold the name of a file in the job's temporary folder, whose name is guaranteed to be unique.

For each global name, an additional global is created (with the suffix _Filename) that hold just the leaf file name of the temporary file.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top level global property list and is accessible from all protocols, but may collide with another property of the same name.

Scoping global properties to the subprotocol where they are used is highly recommended.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help: Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Tempfiles
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma delimited list of global properties, each of which will automatically hold the name of a file in the job's temporary folder, whose name is guaranteed to be unique.

For each global name, an additional global is created (with the suffix _Filename) that hold just the leaf file name of the temporary file.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top level global property list and is accessible from all protocols, but may collide with another property of the same name.

Scoping global properties to the subprotocol where they are used is highly recommended.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help: Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allow the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running local or remote. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required.'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: Comma separated list of maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Applies a PilotScript expression to each data record

PilotScript is the native scripting language in Pipeline Pilot. It is based on PL/SQL and allows you to query or alter the properties on data records. For example, the expression:

A := 10;
creates a property named "A" and sets the value to "10".

For each incoming data record the PilotScript statements in Expression are evaluated.

Notes:

  • To initialize global variables such as counters, use Initial Expression.
  • To clean up global variables or calculate final results use Final Expression.
  • Parameters on Custom Manipulators do not become global variables that can be accessed via @ParameterName syntax. They must be accessed by using the Parameter('ParameterName') function or by using token substitution via $(ParameterName) syntax.

See Also:

  • For more information on PilotScript, see PilotScript Overview.
  • To use PilotScript to filter data records use Custom Filter (PilotScript).

sci:arg.name: Signing Status
sci:arg.sci:help:
The signing status of the experiment. This depends on the type of project assigned to the experiment. There are three types of projects:
  • No signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - no author signature needed
  • Author signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - waiting for author signature
    • Signed - no witness signature needed
  • Author and witness signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - waiting for author signature
    • Signed - waiting for witness signature
    • Rejected by witness
    • Witnessed

sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help: Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allow the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running local or remote. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required.'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: Comma separated list of maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Submission Date Filter
sci:arg.sci:help: Filter by submission date

sci:arg.name: Submission Date Filter Type
sci:arg.sci:help:
Type of filtering. The available choices are:
  • Past Day - Submitted in the last day
  • Past Week - Submitted in the last week
  • Past Month - Submitted in the last month
  • Past Year - Submitted in the last year
  • Custom Range - Submitted in a custom date range

sci:arg.name: Submission Date Filter From Date
sci:arg.sci:help: If using a custom range, the start date of the range.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Submission Date Filter Type') eq 'Custom Range'

sci:arg.name: Submission Date Filter To Date
sci:arg.sci:help: If using a custom range, the end date of the range.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Submission Date Filter Type') eq 'Custom Range'

sci:arg.name: Countersigned Date Filter
sci:arg.sci:help: Filter by the date when the experiment was countersigned (co-signed).

sci:arg.name: Countersigned Date Filter Type
sci:arg.sci:help:
Type of filtering. The available choices are:
  • Past Day - Countersigned in the last day
  • Past Week - Countersigned in the last week
  • Past Month - Countersigned in the last month
  • Past Year - Countersigned in the last year
  • Custom Range - Countersigned in a custom date range

sci:arg.name: Countersigned Date Filter From Date
sci:arg.sci:help: If using a custom range, the start date of the range.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Countersigned Date Filter Type') eq 'Custom Range'

sci:arg.name: Countersigned Date Filter To Date
sci:arg.sci:help: If using a custom range, the end date of the range.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Countersigned Date Filter Type') eq 'Custom Range'

sci:arg.name: Keyword
sci:arg.sci:help: Search by text keyword. If multiple keywords are required, add them on separate lines.

sci:arg.name: Experiment Status
sci:arg.sci:help: The submission status of the experiment.

sci:arg.name: Signing Status
sci:arg.sci:help:
The signing status of the experiment. This depends on the type of project assigned to the experiment. There are three types of projects:
  • No signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - no author signature needed
  • Author signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - waiting for author signature
    • Signed - no witness signature needed
  • Author and witness signature required:
    • Not submitted
    • Submitted - waiting for author signature
    • Signed - waiting for witness signature
    • Rejected by witness
    • Witnessed

sci:arg.name: Experiment Type
sci:arg.sci:help: The experiment type. Enter one per row.

sci:arg.name: Edited Since Date
sci:arg.sci:help: Only retrieve experiments edited since this date.

sci:arg.name: Include Invalid Experiments
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, experiments that have an Errata section with the value Invalid will be included in the query results. The default is to not include these results in any query.

sci:arg.name: Only Current User Experiments
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, only experiments where the current user is the author are retrieved from the database. Note that if a user query is passed in the filter for a user other than the current user, no results will be retrieved.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('This choice is not available when filtering by experiment number.'); not (Parameter('Filter By') eq 'Experiment Number' and Parameter('Filter Type') eq 'Equals')

sci:arg.name: Return Simple Section Data
sci:arg.sci:help: If set to True, simple section data will be returned with the experiment. This data includes the section ID, type and position in the experiment for all sections. Section content will not be returned.

sci:arg.name: Maximum
sci:arg.sci:help: Maximum number of experiments to retrieve. If blank, all experiments that match the query will be retrieved.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('This choice is not available when filtering by experiment number.'); not (Parameter('Filter By') eq 'Experiment Number' and Parameter('Filter Type') eq 'Equals')

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allow the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running local or remote. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid

sci:arg.sci:help: Comma separated list of maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top level global property list and is accessible from all protocols, but may collide with another property of the same name.

Scoping global properties to the subprotocol where they are used is highly recommended.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: Filename
sci:arg.sci:help:
The path of the file or folder to be deleted. Can be a path on the server, an external resource, or a network resource.

  • For a file on or accessible to the server (e.g., via NFS), enter a path.
  • For an external resource, enter resource://resource-name.
  • For a network resource, enter a network URL in the form protocol://server:port/.... (If port is omitted, a default is used.) Protocols supported are:

    • https
    • hdfs (Hadoop Distributed File System)

If the Authentication Method is set to 'Use Username and Password Parameters', then this parameter must be filled in to log into the remote server.

If the Authentication Method is set to 'Use Pipeline Pilot Credentials', then this parameter can be left empty and the logged in username is used. As an override option, if the username is filled in, this username will be used along with the user's Pipeline Pilot password.

sci:arg.name: Recursive
sci:arg.sci:help:
This parameter is only valid if the path provided for the component is a folder. The Recursive parameter is ignored when the target path is for a file.

When the parameter is set to True, then the sub-folders and files will also be deleted.

sci:arg.name: Include Read Only
sci:arg.sci:help: For regular files and folders on Windows servers, this parameter indicates whether files marked by the OS as read only should also be deleted. If this parameter is set to False and the deletion operation fails for some reason, the component will throw an error, depending on the Generate Error on Failure parameter setting.

sci:arg.name: Generate Error on Failure
sci:arg.sci:help:
Set this parameter to True to generate an error message or to False to ignore a failure, when a file or folder is not successfully deleted.

Possible reasons for failure:

  • Deleting a file which is read only, when the Include Read Only parameter is False.
  • Deleting a folder containing files or subfolders, without the Recursive flag set
  • Deleting a folder with the Recursive flag, but which contains a read-only file, while the Include Read Only parameter is False.

sci:arg.name: Script
sci:arg.sci:help:
The Python script to execute. Pipeline Pilot executes the following three subroutines:
  • onInitialize: the subroutine that executes before the first data record is processed.
  • onProcess: the subroutine that executes for each data record.
  • onFinalize: the subroutine that executes after the last data record has been processed.

The ctxt function parameter (and the context facade wrapping it), give access to the environment the component operates in. Data like global variables and the component parameters are accessible via this object.
The dr function parameter and its data facade provide access to the data passed into the component.
sci:arg.sci:value:
import swigpython3 as pilotbase import pilotpython import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET import os
def onInitialize(ctxt): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) return pilotpython.READY_FOR_INPUT_OR_NEW_DATA
def onProcess(ctxt, dr): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) data = pilotpython.DataRecord(dr) props = data.getProperties() # Get the PropertyCollection
try: source_xml_path = context.getComponentParameters().get("Source").getValue().getString().strip() context.debugMessage(f"Source path received: {source_xml_path}") abs_path=context.constructAbsolutePath(source_xml_path) context.debugMessage(f"abs_path:{abs_path}") tree = ET.parse(abs_path) root = tree.getroot()
file_names = [] file_locations = [] name_title = {}
for generic in root.findall('generic'): title = generic.find('XML_title').text eln_value_elem = generic.find('ELN_value') if eln_value_elem is not None: eln_value = eln_value_elem.text if eln_value and '\\' in eln_value: file_name = os.path.basename(eln_value) file_location = eln_value
name_title[file_name]=title file_names.append(file_name) file_locations.append(file_location) section_name = generic.find('XML_title') location = generic.find('ELN_value') location = location.text section_name = section_name.text location = location[0:location.rfind('\\')] location = location[location.find('users'):] # Define properties using the PropertyCollection #props.defineStringProperty("location", location) # Define properties using the PropertyCollection #props.defineStringArrayProperty("FileNames", file_names) #props.defineStringProperty("SectionName", section_name) #context.debugMessage(f"FileNames defined: {file_names}") context.debugMessage(str(name_title)) #props.defineStringArrayProperty("FileLocations", file_locations) props.defineHashTableProperty("file_xmltitle", name_title)
except Exception as e: context.debugMessageError(f"Exception occurred while processing XML: {str(e)}")
return pilotpython.READY_FOR_INPUT_OR_NEW_DATA
def onFinalize(ctxt): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) return None

sci:arg.sci:value: Runs a Python 3 script on the server

The Script parameter already contains a script skeleton with the three functions onInitialize(ctxt), onProcess(ctxt, dr) and onFinalize(ctxt). Those already provide access to the component's environment and the data accessible to it at runtime. To implement the desired functionality, just import any required 3rd party modules, and write functions and glue code to transfer data in and out of Pipeline Pilot. To make 3rd party modules available for import, see the paragraph about Integration of 3rd party modules.

Integration of 3rd party modules

Integration of 3rd party modules is fairly straightforward.
In the case of a pure-Python module, use the PythonPath parameter to specify the module's location.
For modules with binary dependencies (.pyd or .so files), e.g. numpy, or scipy, the solution is platform dependent.
For Linux, one can simply define a shellscript containing an updated LD_LIBRARY_PATH and copy it into the $scitegic/linux_bin/env.d folder. The Pipeline Pilot server will automatically execute that script when creating protocol processes. E.g. a dependency on intel's math library could be resolved with this approach. A more sophisticated version could involve the creation of a custom package, containing a set of specific components and such a script.
For Windows, no action may be necessary. In case the 3rd party module is part of an existing Anaconda distribution on the server, it's possible that a protocol fails with DLL load failed: The specified module could not be found., e.g. when using pillow or numpy. In that case, a fix may simply be to download the offending module's wheel, and reinstalling it into Anaconda with Anaconda's pip. If that is not successful, rebuilding the module using the Python shipped with Pipeline Pilot and integrating it into a Pipeline Pilot package should fix this issue.

Integration of other Pipeline Pilot packages

If your script requires Python modules contained in other Pipeline Pilot packages, use the Use Package parameter. If a Pipeline Pilot package is listed here, the system will query that package's package.conf file for its Python directive and read all applicable PythonPath entries. Packages have to be listed using the vendor/package notation.

See Also:

  • Dynamic Java (on Server)
  • Python Development Guide
  • Python Scripting Component API

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Applies a PilotScript expression to each data record

PilotScript is the native scripting language in Pipeline Pilot. It is based on PL/SQL and allows you to query or alter the properties on data records. For example, the expression:

A := 10;
creates a property named "A" and sets the value to "10".

For each incoming data record the PilotScript statements in Expression are evaluated.

Notes:

  • To initialize global variables such as counters, use Initial Expression.
  • To clean up global variables or calculate final results use Final Expression.
  • Parameters on Custom Manipulators do not become global variables that can be accessed via @ParameterName syntax. They must be accessed by using the Parameter('ParameterName') function or by using token substitution via $(ParameterName) syntax.

See Also:

  • For more information on PilotScript, see PilotScript Overview.
  • To use PilotScript to filter data records use Custom Filter (PilotScript).

sci:arg.name: Script
sci:arg.sci:help:
The Python script to execute. Pipeline Pilot executes the following three subroutines:
  • onInitialize: the subroutine that executes before the first data record is processed.
  • onProcess: the subroutine that executes for each data record.
  • onFinalize: the subroutine that executes after the last data record has been processed.

The ctxt function parameter (and the context facade wrapping it), give access to the environment the component operates in. Data like global variables and the component parameters are accessible via this object.
The dr function parameter and its data facade provide access to the data passed into the component.
sci:arg.sci:value:
import swigpython3 as pilotbase # for bare-metal stuff import pilotpython # nicer python classes from azure.storage.fileshare import ShareServiceClient import os
# Global variables
downloaded_files = [] download_folder = r"E:\Model Data Transfer\DownloadedFile"
def onInitialize(ctxt): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt)
# Ensure download folder exists if not os.path.exists(download_folder): os.makedirs(download_folder)
context.debugMessage("Initialization complete.") return pilotpython.READY_FOR_INPUT_OR_NEW_DATA
def onProcess(ctxt, dr): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) data = pilotpython.DataRecord(dr) props = data.getProperties() selected_files = context.getComponentParameters().get("filesx").getValue().getStringArray() location = context.getComponentParameters().get("location").getValue().getString() global downloaded_files #check = context.getGlobalData('filelist') #context.debugMessage(f"check files: {check}") context.debugMessage(f"slected files: {selected_files}") context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) data = pilotpython.DataRecord(dr) # Azure Storage account credentials account_name = 'bnlwestges01005' account_key = 's5E2TNey9IulqBpxG0pkxeuijPMD4Hw5LgUMK1HnA/VgjNAtI7xbBefCL8r94fL2IvbfEP8OVBzzN4s9vRb2OQ==' share_name = 'rdplp-sbx1' directory_path = location
try: # Connect to Azure File Share service_client = ShareServiceClient( account_url=f"https://{account_name}.file.core.windows.net/", credential=account_key ) share_client = service_client.get_share_client(share_name) directory_client = share_client.get_directory_client(directory_path)
#context.debugMessage(f"Connected to Azure File Share: {share_name}")
for file_name in selected_files: try: context.debugMessage(f"filename: {file_name}") file_client = directory_client.get_file_client(file_name) local_path = os.path.join(download_folder, file_name) with open(local_path, "wb") as file_handle: data_stream = file_client.download_file() file_handle.write(data_stream.readall()) downloaded_files.append(local_path) context.debugMessage(f"Downloaded: {local_path}") except Exception as file_error: context.log(f"Failed to download {file_name}: {file_error}")
except Exception as e: context.debugMessage(f"Azure connection error: {e}")
return pilotpython.READY_FOR_INPUT_OR_NEW_DATA
def onFinalize(ctxt): context = pilotpython.Context(ctxt) context.debugMessage(f"Download complete. Files saved to: {downloaded_files}") return

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Runs a Python 3 script on the server

The Script parameter already contains a script skeleton with the three functions onInitialize(ctxt), onProcess(ctxt, dr) and onFinalize(ctxt). Those already provide access to the component's environment and the data accessible to it at runtime. To implement the desired functionality, just import any required 3rd party modules, and write functions and glue code to transfer data in and out of Pipeline Pilot. To make 3rd party modules available for import, see the paragraph about Integration of 3rd party modules.

Integration of 3rd party modules

Integration of 3rd party modules is fairly straightforward.
In the case of a pure-Python module, use the PythonPath parameter to specify the module's location.
For modules with binary dependencies (.pyd or .so files), e.g. numpy, or scipy, the solution is platform dependent.
For Linux, one can simply define a shellscript containing an updated LD_LIBRARY_PATH and copy it into the $scitegic/linux_bin/env.d folder. The Pipeline Pilot server will automatically execute that script when creating protocol processes. E.g. a dependency on intel's math library could be resolved with this approach. A more sophisticated version could involve the creation of a custom package, containing a set of specific components and such a script.
For Windows, no action may be necessary. In case the 3rd party module is part of an existing Anaconda distribution on the server, it's possible that a protocol fails with DLL load failed: The specified module could not be found., e.g. when using pillow or numpy. In that case, a fix may simply be to download the offending module's wheel, and reinstalling it into Anaconda with Anaconda's pip. If that is not successful, rebuilding the module using the Python shipped with Pipeline Pilot and integrating it into a Pipeline Pilot package should fix this issue.

Integration of other Pipeline Pilot packages

If your script requires Python modules contained in other Pipeline Pilot packages, use the Use Package parameter. If a Pipeline Pilot package is listed here, the system will query that package's package.conf file for its Python directive and read all applicable PythonPath entries. Packages have to be listed using the vendor/package notation.

See Also:

  • Dynamic Java (on Server)
  • Python Development Guide
  • Python Scripting Component API

sci:arg.name: File Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
Options for choosing which files to emit.

For example, you can limit files to those matching a particular suffix (e.g., *.pdf), or only those that have been modified since a previous run of this component.

sci:arg.name: FilePattern
sci:arg.sci:help: Only watch files with a name matching this pattern (e.g., *.pdf)

sci:arg.name: FindNewFiles
sci:arg.sci:help: Emit files that have not been previously emitted by this component and logged to the log file.

sci:arg.name: FindModifiedFiles
sci:arg.sci:help: Emit files that have been previously emitted (and logged) by this component, but which have also been modified since then.

sci:arg.name: CheckExistingFiles
sci:arg.sci:help: If True, scan the directory for files. This is the typical usage. However, you may set this false when CheckMissingFiles is true in order to only check for missing files.

sci:arg.name: CheckMissingFiles
sci:arg.sci:help: Check whether files were deleted that have been previously emitted (and logged) by this component. Any deleted files will be emitted on the Fail Port, and the property DocFileMissing will be set to True.

sci:arg.name: Logging Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
Options for controlling the log file.

By default, no logging is performed by this component. It is deferred to Directory Watcher Logger, a component which you must add to your protocol after this component and after you have processed the file. It is preferable to defer logging so that files are only logged if they are successfully processed by your protocol.

sci:arg.name: Log Action
sci:arg.sci:help:
Files emitted by this component may be logged. Logging allows this component to read a directory repeatedly, and only output files that are new or have been changed or deleted since the last run.

Choices are:

  • Immediate: logging occurs as the component traverses the file system; therefore, a file may be logged before it is emitted by the component, for example, if the protocol terminates early (due to error) or the component itself fails (due to a file system irregularity)
  • On Emit: logging occurs as each file is emitted by the component
  • Defer: logging is not performed by this component, but the record contains the log info necessary to be logged later by Directory Watcher Logger
  • Silent: no logging and no info is generated

sci:arg.name: LogFile
sci:arg.sci:help:
The file that records the names and timestamps of files that have been processed.

Note: The file name may be either an absolute path to a file or a relative path. If relative, then the value of LogDirectory is used if it is defined, otherwise the log file is created relative to the user's public directory on the Pipeline Pilot server.

sci:arg.name: LogDirectory
sci:arg.sci:help: Path to a directory where the log file is stored

sci:arg.name: ResetLogFile
sci:arg.sci:help: Reset the record of processed files

sci:arg.name: RewriteLogFile
sci:arg.sci:help: If true and the log file exists from a previous run, rewrite the log file to compact redundant entries

sci:arg.name: Output Options
sci:arg.sci:help: Options for defining the output of the component.

sci:arg.name: URLPattern
sci:arg.sci:help:
A string pattern which creates a URL to each file. For example:

http://myserver/fetch.cgi?file=${filepathenc}

You may include one or more substitution strings in your pattern. Each such string will be replaced by the applicable value for the given emitted file. Substitution strings are of the form ${key}, where key is one of the following:

  • filename: the name of the file
  • filenameenc: the name of the file, URL-encoded
  • filepath: the full path to the file
  • filepathenc: the full path the the file, URL-encoded
  • directory: the full path to the directory containing the file
  • directoryenc: the full path to the directory containing the file, URL-encoded
  • relativepath: the path to the file relative to the watched directory
  • relativepathenc: the path to the file relative to the watched directory, URL-encoded

sci:arg.name: URLPrefix
sci:arg.sci:help:
For remote access to each file via a web browser, the URLPrefix is pre-pended to the pathname of the file (relative to Directory).

Note: URLPrefix is applicable only if URLPattern is not defined. If neither URLPrefix nor URLPattern is defined, then the URL is defined using the Pipeline Pilot server DownloadFile service.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: Parameter( 'URLPattern' ) eq ''

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help:
Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.

 

Note: In an expression inside the subprotocol you can identify the category property name as:

      parentproperty('RunToCompletion Categorize Using')

And so to access the value of this property on the current data record, use:

      property(parentproperty('RunToCompletion Categorize Using'))
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allows the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running locally or remotely. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option with care, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. Generally speaking, it yields improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma-separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (that is, server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be useful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required.'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: A comma-separated list of the maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.</br></br>For non-Grid Engine job, the number of jobs will be limited to the value for the maximum number of simultaneous subprotocol jobs as defined in the Admin Console even if this value is higher than the value entered here or '*'.</br></br>For Grid Engine jobs, the number of jobs will be limited to the value for the maximum number of simultaneous subprotocol grid jobs as defined in the Admin Console even if this value is higher than the value entered here or '*'.</br></br>
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:help: Run subprotocol on grid engine if available. Note: If no grid engine is configured the subprotocol will still run even if this parameter is set to true.
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Queue Name
Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Grid Options
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Queue Name
sci:arg.sci:help: Select the queue name on the grid to submit jobs to. Leave blank to use default queue name.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid Grid Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
This is an array of command line options to send to the Grid engine submit command.

If you just include one line, whatever you enter will be sent "as is" to the submission command.


Example - Just sending options directly to command line - PBS

-l procs=16 -l walltime=08:00:00 -A PROJECTID


There are a number of parameters that Pipeline Pilot will translate to the correct command line options for whichever supported Grid Engine you are using.


Example - Supported parameters

Account=<Project/Account name>

Maximum Execution Time=<HH:MM:SS> hours, minutes, seconds - LSF ignores seconds

Number of Cores=<16>

Number of GPUs=<4>

Parallel Environment=<The Parallel Environment to use> - Only needed for SGE

Other=<Additional Parameters sent directly to submit command line>


Any of these options can be commented out by placing a # in front of them.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: parameter('Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Preserve Order
sci:arg.sci:help: Whether to preserve the order of the data as it enters and leaves the remote subprotocol.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Tempfiles
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma-delimited list of global properties, each of which is automatically populated with the name of a file in the job's temporary folder, which always has a unique name.

For each global name, an additional global is created (with the suffix _Filename) that hold only the leaf file name of the temporary file.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Separate property names with commas. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top-level global property list and is accessible from all subprotocols, but breaks the encapsulation of the subprotocol and may collide with another property of the same name.

Therefore, you should always declare a new global property in the DeclareLocal parameter, to minimize the scope of the global property to the subprotocol where it is used.

The example DeclareLocal value below creates 3 global properties in the subprotocol scope. Note that you can initialize the declared global value with a scalar value using the ":=" syntax, as shown. You can surround text string values with quotes to aid clarity.

    SubP_Counter := 0, SubP_NameHash, SubP_TitleText:="Sample 1"

sci:arg.name: ComponentHelp
sci:arg.sci:value: Applies a PilotScript expression to each data record

PilotScript is the native scripting language in Pipeline Pilot. It is based on PL/SQL and allows you to query or alter the properties on data records. For example, the expression:

A := 10;
creates a property named "A" and sets the value to "10".

For each incoming data record the PilotScript statements in Expression are evaluated.

Notes:

  • To initialize global variables such as counters, use Initial Expression.
  • To clean up global variables or calculate final results use Final Expression.
  • Parameters on Custom Manipulators do not become global variables that can be accessed via @ParameterName syntax. They must be accessed by using the Parameter('ParameterName') function or by using token substitution via $(ParameterName) syntax.

See Also:

  • For more information on PilotScript, see PilotScript Overview.
  • To use PilotScript to filter data records use Custom Filter (PilotScript).

sci:arg.name: Tempfiles
sci:arg.sci:help:
A comma delimited list of global properties, each of which will automatically hold the name of a file in the job's temporary folder, whose name is guaranteed to be unique.

For each global name, an additional global is created (with the suffix _Filename) that hold just the leaf file name of the temporary file.

sci:arg.name: DeclareLocal
sci:arg.sci:help:
Lists a set of properties (without the @) to create on the global property list for this subprotocol. Such properties can only be accessed within the scope of this subprotocol and its descendent subprotocols.

Any global property not declared in this way is created on the top level global property list and is accessible from all protocols, but may collide with another property of the same name.

Scoping global properties to the subprotocol where they are used is highly recommended.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion
sci:arg.sci:help:
When RunToCompletion is set to "True - For Each Data Record", the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each individual data record it processes.

When set to "True - For Each Category", the data records are divided into categories based on the value of the Categorize Using parameter and then the subprotocol is re-initialized and executed in its entirety for each category of data records. When used in conjunction with Parallel Processing Options, each category of data records will be sent to the remote server as part of one single batch.

sci:arg.name: RunToCompletion Categorize Using
sci:arg.sci:help: Required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category, this parameter specifies the property or properties used to define the categories.
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required when RunToCompletion is set to True - For Each Category'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To Enable, Set RunToCompletion to True - For Each Category'); Parameter('RunToCompletion') eq 'True - For Each Category';

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options
sci:arg.sci:help:
When set to True, this set of options allow the subprotocol to execute in parallel on one or more independent Pipeline Pilot servers, running local or remote. Additional parameters control the number of data records to send in each process batch, the list of Pipeline Pilot servers to use, the number of protocol processes that can be executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

Use this option judiciously, since it will not increase throughput in all circumstances. In general, it will yield improved performance when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. As a rough guide, performance can be improved when each individual batch requires at least 10 seconds to execute, although this can be affected by the size of each data record.

When running the protocol with debugging, the subprotocol will provide debugging messages to detail each of the various steps of execution. Also, components located within the parallel subprotocol will display their debugging messages as well.

For more information on the parallel subprotocol options, see Parallel Processing Subprotocols.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Batch Size
sci:arg.sci:help:
The number of records to send to the remote server(s) for each subprotocol execution. In general, performance is optimized when the amount of time required to process each batch is at least 10 seconds (note that this can vary depending on the characteristics of the remote server's hardware). Use a batch size of -1 to pass all data in a single batch.

When RunToCompletion is set to "True - for each category", the batch sizes will be determined by the number of records in each individual category. Therefore, the Batch Size parameter is not applicable.

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server
sci:arg.sci:help:
Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers on which to execute the parallel subprotocol. The server names should be in the same format as the Pipeline Pilot Client's change server dialog (server-name:port-number).

Specifying localhost as a server will cause the subprotocol to use its own Pipeline Pilot server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where 'localhost' requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).
sci:arg.sci:member: Parallel Processing Options Server Run On Grid
sci:arg.sci:validscript: SetInvalidDetails('This parameter is required.'); Parameter() ne '';
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Parallel Processing Options Server Processes
sci:arg.sci:help: Comma separated list of maximum number of batches that can be simultaneously executed on each remote server. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. If '*' is specified as the number of processes, then that server will only launch as many batches as the administrator of the remote server has permitted.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("This parameter is only applicable if 'Parallel Processing Options' is 'True'"); Parameter('Parallel Processing Options');

sci:arg.name: Filename
sci:arg.sci:help:
The path of the file or folder to be deleted. Can be a path on the server, an external resource, or a network resource.

  • For a file on or accessible to the server (e.g., via NFS), enter a path.
  • For an external resource, enter resource://resource-name.
  • For a network resource, enter a network URL in the form protocol://server:port/.... (If port is omitted, a default is used.) Protocols supported are:
    • http
    • https
    • hdfs (Hadoop Distributed File System)

sci:arg.name: Filename Authentication Options
sci:arg.sci:help: For HTTP and HTTPS sources, you may optionally specify authentication information for the URL in the following parameters.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To enable, specify an HTTP URL for the Filename'); Parameter('Filename') rlike '^(https?|hdfs):';

sci:arg.name: Filename Authentication Options Authentication Method
sci:arg.sci:help:
Determines which method to use during authentication with an HTTP or HTTPS URL.
  • Use Username and Password Parameters: Use the values provided by the component Filename parameter group's Username and Password parameters.
  • Use Pipeline Pilot Credentials: Use the username and password that were provided when the user logged into Pipeline Pilot. NOTE: if the Username parameter is provided, its value will override the user's logged in username.

sci:arg.name: Filename Authentication Options Username
sci:arg.sci:help:
The username used to connect to the supplied URL Filename.

If the Authentication Method is set to 'Use Username and Password Parameters', then this parameter must be filled in to log into the remote server.

If the Authentication Method is set to 'Use Pipeline Pilot Credentials', then this parameter can be left empty and the logged in username is used. As an override option, if the username is filled in, this username will be used along with the user's Pipeline Pilot password.

sci:arg.name: Filename Authentication Options Password
sci:arg.sci:help: The password used to authenticate with the Filename server. This parameter is disabled if Authentication Method is not set to 'Use Username and Password Parameters'.
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails("To enable, set Authentication Method to 'Use Username and Password Parameters'"); Parameter('Filename Authentication Options Authentication Method') eq 'Use Username and Password Parameters';

sci:arg.name: Filename Authentication Options KDC Server
sci:arg.sci:help: When connecting to an HDFS URL, KDC Server and Realm are also required
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To enable, specify an HDFS URL for the Filename'); Parameter('Filename') rlike '^hdfs:';

sci:arg.name: Filename Authentication Options KDC Realm
sci:arg.sci:help: When connecting to an HDFS URL, KDC Server and Realm are also required
sci:arg.sci:enabledscript: SetDisabledDetails('To enable, specify an HDFS URL for the Filename'); Parameter('Filename') rlike '^hdfs:';

sci:arg.name: Recursive
sci:arg.sci:help:
This parameter is only valid if the path provided for the component is a folder. The Recursive parameter is ignored when the target path is for a file.

When the parameter is set to True, then the sub-folders and files will also be deleted.

sci:arg.name: Include Read Only
sci:arg.sci:help: For regular files and folders on Windows servers, this parameter indicates whether files marked by the OS as read only should also be deleted. If this parameter is set to False and the deletion operation fails for some reason, the component will throw an error, depending on the Generate Error on Failure parameter setting.

sci:arg.name: Generate Error on Failure
sci:arg.sci:help:
Set this parameter to True to generate an error message or to False to ignore a failure, when a file or folder is not successfully deleted.

Possible reasons for failure:

  • Deleting a file which is read only, when the Include Read Only parameter is False.
  • Deleting a folder containing files or subfolders, without the Recursive flag set
  • Deleting a folder with the Recursive flag, but which contains a read-only file, while the Include Read Only parameter is False.
